Polianthes tuberosa

Rajnigandha — white, creamy and almost narcotic.

How to use

  • One drop, diluted into a carrier. Never neat.
  • Keep to 0.5% — above that it stops being pleasant.
  • Blend with sandalwood if you want to soften it.

Dilute before applying to skin and patch-test first. Not for internal use.

Scent profile

  • Creamy white floral
  • Green sap
  • Waxy sweetness

What's in it

  • 100% Polianthes tuberosa flower absolute

Who it's for

People who love heavy florals

If jasmine and ylang ylang appeal, tuberose is the furthest point in that direction.

Anyone who grew up with rajnigandha

The flower sold on every Indian street corner, concentrated to an extraordinary degree.

Perfume blenders

A heart note with genuine weight, used in trace amounts.

What people get wrong

Treating it like a floral essential oil. Tuberose is unusually heavy even among absolutes, and a blend that smells balanced in the bottle can be overwhelming an hour later.

Buying it as a gift without checking. It is among the most polarising scents in perfumery — people either adore it or find it suffocating, and there is rarely a middle position.

What it won't do

An absolute, solvent extracted, so trace residue is inherent to the process. Tuberose cannot be steam distilled at all — the heat destroys it.

It is not a subtle material and no dilution makes it subtle. It makes it bearable.

We describe how our oils smell and how people use them. We don't make medical claims, because essential oils aren't medicine.

Questions about Tuberose (Rajnigandha) Absolute

Is rajnigandha the same as tuberose?

Yes. Rajnigandha is the Indian name for Polianthes tuberosa, the flower sold in garlands and bunches across the country. The absolute is extracted from those same blooms.

Why is there no tuberose essential oil?

The flower cannot survive distillation — heat destroys the compounds that make it smell the way it does. Solvent extraction is the only method that captures it, which is why every tuberose on the market is an absolute.

How long does it keep once opened?

Two to three years stored properly — cool, dark and tightly closed. Distilled oils keep considerably better than cold-pressed citrus.

What dilution should I use on skin?

Lower than most. An absolute, not an essential oil — solvent extracted, so trace residue is inherent. Avoid during pregnancy. For general use, dilute into a carrier oil such as jojoba and patch-test on a small area first.

Can I take it internally?

No. None of our oils are food grade and none are sold for internal use. Essential oils are extremely concentrated, and advice to add them to water or food is not advice we endorse.

How quickly will it arrive?

Orders are dispatched from Delhi within two business days and usually arrive within a further three to five, depending on where you are. Shipping is free over ₹999.
